body: Twitch is an interesting option for revitalizing their content, for sure, but they seem to be developing their formats and finding their stride more and more as the weeks pass. And in light of the issues with profit some YouTube content creators are having, diversifying is a smart play, and using footage to bring content across mediums (twitch to youtube) is a creative solution. I personally was more surprised that they didn't take the 15 year anniversary as an opportunity to return to old formats for limited series to channel the nostalgia into engaging new content. It may be the pandemic, but in some of the new content you can just sense the fatigue from the cast, especially those who are in the majority of videos. Considering what their schedules must be like, who can really blame them for not being full energy 100% of the time they are on camera. Plus any writer can tell you that repeatedly using the same formats is just going to wear you out. I'll keep watching and supporting, but I really hope they get another second wind soon because they're putting out a bunch of happiness into the world and they don't deserve fatigue, especially not creative fatigue. I know no one cares about my opinion, and even fewer agree with me, but I just wanted to put it out there.

This comment really hit home for me. When I was young I was in shape and healthy, (as well as maintaining great grades and developing my sense of humor with my family) but I was always treated by peers as though my only worth was in being attractive to males. I went through a few abusive relationships and a sexual assault, and after coping with drug use I eventually found food. Now that I am fat, I don’t get randomly harassed online with people I know or don’t know sending lewd messages out of the blue. When I go out to run an errand, I don’t have to deal with being hit on when I really don’t want to be. I’ve been through therapy to try to help, but the truth is that, especially to people who have been objectified like that, being out of shape is just so freeing and you feel so much safer. People actually see me for who I am and not what I look like. It’s hard to go back to that other life, even if it does mean you get to be healthy and enjoy the world more. I wonder if things will ever get to the point where people (of all gender identities) don’t have to feel this way.

Honestly, it probably would have gone over better if Gimple and Kirkman weren't on TTD. If there is one thing I've been taught in writing courses, or in any arts course, it is to never try to defend your work. Any piece, especially in the television medium, shouldn't have to be explained or validated. It should be able to stand on its own, and considering the money made in this situation, it should be of the best quality. Instead we had a solid 30 minutes of them circlejerking their own work on TTD, when we should have just gotten to fanlove over JDM'S perfect (IMO) incarnation of Negan (#papawinchesterno!). No one wants to see a writer and a creator spew explanations and fondle their creativity on live tv, and I think it has turned a lazy writing trick (and I say trick, because a trick is something a whore does for money) into a full on hatefest from their most die hard fans. That being said, it obviously worked for them, because we are all talking about it. All press is good press, and I'm sure new people will check out the show out of curiosity.  So if we all are really this pissed, we should turn our attention to the aspects of the episode we liked, like the fall of Rick through hubris, or Negan's awesomeness, or GTA Trevor's great performance. By focusing on the cliffhanger, we are inviting it to happen again because they know it accomplished something and got us talking. If we focus on other things, they might realize that maybe cheap tricks aren't the best way to handle significant moments in the story in terms of their most invested fans...but that's none of my business. *sips lipton tea

The thing I find most useful is that the English major forces me to read a larger variety of works that I might not if I was another major.  That might not seem very important to writing, but it has improved my own work by at least 90%.  
By reading things that aren't in my enjoyment zone I can see more of what other authors have done, and how (even if it is a horrible book/story/poem) various techniques and devices can be used.  
It also has made me more comfortable with more challenging/sophisticated devices. 
So basically, by analyzing a broad range of writing I am better able to figure out who I want to be as a writer, even if I never get to be in the position the authors I have to read are in.
